_comment: The parameter points each task is MEASURED at by score/points.py, besides the scored one. UNTRUSTED and not hashed by the checker: this is measurement only. Every proof holds at every point of the task's range, so a point here is the same proved design at other parameters; the ranked board stays at task.json's scoring.params, which must be one of the points (score/test_points.py checks it). The numbers are written to score/measured/<task>.json, which the site reads ('measured, not ranked').

Per task: `points`, each {params, label?}: `label` names a multi-parameter point ('binary32'); without one the site writes 'N = 8'. `scale`: the parameter the scaling view puts on its x axis (default: the task's only parameter), `scale_label` the axis title. `families`: fixed-size baselines generated once per size (one file per point), drawn as one line of the scaling view under the family's name. `skip`: (design, point) pairs that are not measured, each with the reason and the measurement it rests on.

The designs: every proved reference of task.json, every baseline of tests/expected.json (a baseline with `banlist_points` is a fixed-size design and is measured at those points only), and with `--records` the players' leaderboard records. Together they cover every design of score/tests/ppa/designs.json (checked). A point other than the scored one whose flow fails or does not finish within the task's time limit (task.json `time_limit_s`) is dropped for that design and the data says so; the scored point has no limit beyond the pinned flow's own.
